name: עֵבֶר
gloss: the region beyond, the other side
summary: Chiefly Eber son of Shelah, great-grandson of Shem, whom Genesis singles out: Shem is “the father of all the sons of Eber” (Gen 10:21). In his son Peleg's days the earth was divided (Gen 10:25); Eber lived 34 years and begot Peleg, and 430 years after (Gen 11:16–17). He stands in the line from Shem to Abraham (1Ch 1:25) and so in Luke's genealogy of Jesus (Luk 3:35), and Balaam names “Eber” beside Asshur as a people to be afflicted (Num 24:24). The name is the noun עֵבֶר “the side across, the region beyond”; scripture does not say why he was so named. Four other men bear it: a Gadite (1Ch 5:13), two Benjamites (1Ch 8:12, 22) and a priest of the return (Neh 12:20).

evidence.note: “To Shem also, the father of all the sons of Eber (כָּל בְּנֵי עֵבֶר), the elder brother of Japheth, children were born.”
“To Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided, and his brother's name was Joktan.”
Shelah begot Eber; Eber lived thirty-four years and begot Peleg, and after he begot Peleg four hundred and thirty years.
“Eber, Peleg, Reu”: the line of Shem to Abram.
“Ships from Kittim will afflict Asshur and afflict Eber (וְעִנּוּ עֵבֶר).”
Ἔβερ in the genealogy of Jesus.
“Of Amok, Eber”: head of a priestly house in the days of Joiakim.
The noun the name is: “your fathers dwelt beyond the River (בְּעֵבֶר הַנָּהָר)”.

note: Takes p.ah.ac. Its tokens as the brief counts them (32) include many עֵבֶר “side, beyond” filed under this key by spelling (Exo 25:37; Deu 4:49; 1Ki 5:4 and others); the man and the men are Gen 10:21, 24, 25; 11:14–17; Num 24:24; 1Ch 1:18, 19, 25; 5:13; 8:12, 22; Neh 12:20. The gentilic עִבְרִי “Hebrew” (p.ah.ad) is kept in the root entry avar as a word, not here: TIPNR gives the Hebrews a group record of their own (Hebrews@Gen.14.13), and a people takes no name entry. Gen 10:21 can be read of Eber the man or of “the sons of Eber” as a people (as Num 24:24); both are kept. The New Testament spells him Ἔβερ (Luk 3:35).
